entry.name: testing-pyramid
entry.role: Five-level testing pyramid (DNA-66, RFC-0823): L1 unit (vitest), L2 integration (vitest against dev-deployed Workers), L3 contract (Zod schema validation), L4 E2E (Playwright against dev-deployed sites), L5 smoke (post-deploy health checks). All test definitions live in `packages/werkstatt-site/src/testing/`. The dev channel is the canonical test environment.

dependency-rules.rule: Apps may consume packages through stable public APIs rather than package-private internals.
Framework adapters depend on the framework-free core, not the other way around.
Cross-workspace changes must preserve explicit ownership boundaries between routes, content, config, styles, scripts, and semantic outputs.
Version constraints and compatibility assumptions should be recorded here when they become architectural dependencies rather than local package trivia.
`packages/ontology` owns the canonical RFC-0071 biome and site-family contracts; validators and codegen must consume those schemas rather than duplicating them locally.
`packages/tokens` owns the canonical `--ds-*` names that biome validators and biome CSS generation may emit; token-name mapping must stay synchronized with `TOKEN_NAMES`.

Every authored relative import/export in `packages/**/*.ts(x)` uses the on-disk `.ts` / `.tsx` extension. `tsconfig/base.json` enables `allowImportingTsExtensions`; `tsconfig/node-lib.json` rewrites emitted relative imports to `.js` for build-backed packages.

Build-backed packages may export runtime from `dist/*.js` and types from `dist/*.d.ts`; source-consumed package surfaces may export raw `src/*.ts` / `.astro` when consumers require source access. The package export target does not change the authored local-import rule.
Generator-owned app files follow their owning template and Astro/Vite runtime contract. Import-style changes to generated app files belong in the generator/template first, followed by regeneration.

`packages/surface` owns the `BlueprintLevel` contract including the optional `pillar` field (RFC-0490). `packages/share` owns the `SemanticPageType` union including `"collection"` (RFC-0490) and the `collectionItems` field on `SemanticPageModel`. `packages/ontology` owns the Zod schema mirror that validates `pillar` and `"collection"` at blueprint load time. The baker in `packages/os/site-kernel-checks` reads `pillar` from the level — it must not duplicate pillar content in TypeScript.

ai-facing-format-rules.rule: For large AI-facing context, plans, reports, and knowledge graphs, prefer XML documents in `docs/`.
Do not replace working machine config formats required by tools; Compass XML applies to semantic/project context, not to tool-native config files.
When adding structured logs or reports for AI analysis, keep block names stable and aligned with module contracts or semantic anchors.

command-policy.rule: Prefer repository-root commands with `pnpm --filter <workspace> ...` for scoped work.
Use `turbo run ...` only when the task intentionally spans multiple workspaces.
Validate the smallest affected surface first, then expand only when shared boundaries changed.
Register workspace-scoped site OS commands in the repository root `tools/kernel.config.ts`; keep app-local `tools/kernel.config.ts` files focused on app-scoped modules and pipelines.

rules.rule: Shared Compass automation must stay app-agnostic and run from the workspace root.
Inventory and validation commands may write machine-readable XML artifacts under `docs/` but must not silently rewrite authored source files.
Backfill or mutation automation should be added only after inventory and validation surfaces are stable and idempotent.
Agents MUST NOT trigger npm publish without an explicit operator command.
All extraction configs MUST include excludePathSegments: [".npmrc"] to prevent token leakage.
Breaking engine major requires all plugin packages to be republished simultaneously.

control-plane.law-kernel: Non-replaceable authority for graph admission, lifecycle, effects, isolation, certification, and promotion.
control-plane.governance: `forge/program@1` packet control plane specified by RFC-0856; documentation-only until packet 000.

component-plane.profile: Exactly one stack profile identity per workshop.
component-plane.graph: Immutable resolved set of versioned capabilities with explicit grants, effects, scopes, isolation, and resource bounds.
component-plane.stacks: `@warpgogol/werkstatt-site`, `@warpgogol/werkstatt-game`, and `@warpgogol/werkstatt-video` remain stack-side providers and never become engine dependencies.

security-plane.rule: Untrusted executable workloads use only an independently admitted real sandbox and deny-by-default broker; vm, workers, and ordinary subprocesses are not security tiers.
Release candidates and capability candidates remain distinct content-addressed artifacts.
Promotion requires deterministic, held-out, regression, independent evaluation, shadow, canary, and observation evidence under Law Kernel authority.

certification-plane.rule: Strict Zod schemas with `.strict()` validation own all CERT-001 certification object types; no parallel interfaces or compatibility aliases.
Identity builders construct fresh payloads field-by-field, snapshot through RFC-0849, and hash through the engine fingerprint owner; no clone/delete or generic hash.
Evidence identity enforces redaction closure before construction; unresolved secrets or PII fail with CERT-REDACTION-01.
No evaluation algorithms, state cutover, storage, commands, producers, adapters, authority execution, or deployment logic exists in the contracts module.
Evidence index is built once per decision in O(E) time; selection uses authority admission sequence and immutable evaluation cuts — timestamps, filenames, and input order never establish precedence.

Aggregation preserves per-requirement pass/fail/stale/incomplete/not-applicable, applies precedence fail > stale > incomplete > pass, and never infers pass from empty profile, zero diagnostics, or unknown values.
Action packs create one anchored task per actionable non-pass requirement with topological ordering and cycle detection; missing anchors or verification commands fail with CERT-ACTION-01.
Dossier root hashing is order-sensitive and location/projection-time independent.
Hard limits: 1,000 requirements, 10,000 evidence records, 1,000 action tasks — overflow returns explicit non-pass failures without truncation.
Evaluation modules have no filesystem/network/clock/env/plugin imports and mutate none of their inputs.

Release manifests accept only artifact readiness states `prepared` and `ready` (RFC-0851); legacy deployment-state labels are rejected without translation. All Leitstand commands and `release.rollback` are blocked with `CERT-TRANSITION-01` until CERT-007.

RFC-0848 integration suite at `packages/werkstatt/src/tests/certification-foundation.integration.test.ts` proves ten cross-module CERT-INTEGRATION laws using public child APIs only — no child logic is reimplemented, no adapters/aliases/fallback passes are introduced, and `@warpgogol/werkstatt` imports no stack plugin.

CERT-002 profile schemas at `packages/werkstatt/src/certification/profile/` own `CertificationProfileV1` with strict Zod validation, producer declarations, requirements, applicability, reuse/freshness, remediation, retention, and evaluator policy. Canonical hash uses RFC-0849 fingerprint authority. `validateCertificationProfileV1` enforces plugin/profile binding, duplicate IDs, producer registration, nine-dimension Main gate coverage, continuous-health freshness, and rollback eligibility. No producer execution or deployment decisions.

CERT-003 authority at `packages/werkstatt/src/certification/authority/` owns issuer registry with idempotent add, conflicting-key rejection, attestation verification, and signed decision/root verification. Storage at `packages/werkstatt/src/certification/storage/` owns the content-addressed dossier repository with append-only event chain, previousEventHash chain validation, root hash recomputation via RFC-0849, provider-neutral adapter interface, in-memory adapter, stored-object verification, retention GC with protected references and age thresholds, tombstones, and durable replica root-hash verification. No R2 adapter, producer orchestration, or deployment commands.

CERT-004 orchestration at `packages/werkstatt/src/certification/orchestration/` owns producer dependency planning (topological sort with cycle detection, duplicate/unknown dependency rejection), gate lock manager (per-release+gate mutual exclusion, idempotent re-acquire, concurrent rejection), producer execution with bounded parallelism (semaphore), timeout, retry with backoff, progress events, and resume point computation from partial evidence. Commands at `packages/werkstatt/src/certification/commands/` own read-only `getCertificationStatus` and `verifyCertification` (candidate ID recompute, dossier integrity, root hash match, decision references). No producer implementations, deployment commands, or I/O imports.

CERT-005 producers at `packages/werkstatt/src/certification/producers/` owns the deterministic producer framework — typed producer registry with duplicate rejection (`CERT-PRODUCER-01`), profile validation (`CERT-PRODUCER-03`/`CERT-PRODUCER-04`), applicability evaluation (always/entitlement/config/surface), false-pass guard rejecting empty-result success (`CERT-PRODUCER-05`), summary-only warning success (`CERT-PRODUCER-06`), and grace-period success (`CERT-PRODUCER-07`), diagnostic normalization with deduplication (`CERT-PRODUCER-08`), route/state/viewport matrix planning, and producer execution with evidence envelope construction (`CERT-PRODUCER-09`/`CERT-PRODUCER-10`/`CERT-PRODUCER-11`). No site-specific producer implementations, deployment commands, or I/O imports.

CERT-006 evaluators at `packages/werkstatt/src/certification/evaluators/` owns the independent evaluator framework — evaluator registry with duplicate rejection (`CERT-EVAL-01`), risk routing (ordinary/critical/borderline with dimension-matched rules, 1 evaluator for ordinary, 2 for critical/borderline), evaluator isolation rejecting self-review (`CERT-EVAL-02`) and duplicate identities (`CERT-EVAL-03`), consensus aggregation (pass/pass → pass, fail/fail → fail, disagreement/missing → incomplete), payload validation (`CERT-EVAL-07` bundle hash, `CERT-EVAL-08` rubric, `CERT-EVAL-09` confidence, `CERT-EVAL-10` criterion/rationale), evaluator execution (`CERT-EVAL-11` isolation, `CERT-EVAL-12` unregistered, `CERT-EVAL-13` crash/invalid), and coverage manifest building from deterministic evidence. No evaluator-led mutation, human approval, or I/O imports.

RFC-0863 capability artifacts at `packages/werkstatt/src/capability-artifacts/` owns the immutable content-addressed artifact store with size/media-type policy (`CERT-ARTIFACT-01`/`CERT-ARTIFACT-02`), immutability (`CERT-ARTIFACT-03`), hash verification (`CERT-ARTIFACT-04`/`CERT-ARTIFACT-05`), and provider admission store (`CERT-ARTIFACT-06` non-pass, `CERT-ARTIFACT-07` stale conformance). Capability broker at `packages/werkstatt/src/isolation/broker/` owns the deny-by-default bridge — ambient host access rejection (`CERT-BROKER-01`), duplicate capability rejection (`CERT-BROKER-02`), policy/grant enforcement, size/concurrency limits, and redacted audit. Sandbox providers at `packages/werkstatt/src/isolation/providers/` owns concrete adapter implementations with all 12 required property evidence. No evolution controller, canary promotion, or provider-specific manifest field.

RFC-0864 evolution controller at `packages/werkstatt/src/evolution/` owns the governed capability evolution — forward-only sequence `defined → tested → shadowed → canary → promoted` with rollback and quarantine as compensating transitions. Reducer enforces monotonic stage transitions, idempotency keys, sequence numbers, kill switch (`CERT-EVO-01`), and evidence requirements per stage. Guards enforce self-change boundary for forbidden scopes (`CERT-EVO-GUARD-01`), evidence immutability (`CERT-EVO-GUARD-02`/`03`), authority expiry (`CERT-EVO-GUARD-05`), shadow side effects (`CERT-EVO-GUARD-06`), canary boundaries (`CERT-EVO-GUARD-07`/`08`/`09`), and evidence poisoning (`CERT-EVO-GUARD-10`/`11`). Controller cannot change Law Kernel, permissions, effect/isolation contracts, canonical identities/diagnostics, controller code, or evaluator policy.

CERT-007 deployment effect authority at `packages/werkstatt/src/certification/deployment/` owns signed external-effect authorization for Dev, Alt, and Main channel transitions. Gate requirements (`DEPLOYMENT_GATE_REQUIREMENTS`) enforce no force/skip/waiver/grace bypass paths. `authorizeDeployment` rejects unknown gates (`CERT-DEPLOY-01`), force (`CERT-DEPLOY-02`), skip (`CERT-DEPLOY-03`), waiver (`CERT-DEPLOY-04`), grace (`CERT-DEPLOY-05`), candidate mismatch (`CERT-DEPLOY-06`), non-pass gate decision (`CERT-DEPLOY-07`), missing artifact readiness (`CERT-DEPLOY-08`), and missing durable sync for Alt/Main (`CERT-DEPLOY-09`). `verifyMainPromotion` rejects candidate mismatch (`CERT-DEPLOY-10`), non-pass verification (`CERT-DEPLOY-11`), and missing durable sync (`CERT-DEPLOY-12`). `evaluateRollback` denies rollback during shared outage, when artifact is not ready, or when target is the same candidate. `evaluateCrashRecovery` resumes verification, restarts deployment, or quarantines with ambiguous state detection (`CERT-DEPLOY-13`). No success inference from deploy exit alone, no false Main success from incomplete verification.

CERT-008 continuous health at `packages/werkstatt/src/certification/health/` owns monitoring windows, health state transitions, drift classification, and incident response. `evaluateHealth` returns current (all pass), degraded (fail/stale/incomplete), with `CERT-HEALTH-01` for empty results. `shouldRevoke` checks consecutive degraded windows against threshold. `classifyDriftCause` identifies shared outage, expired evidence, candidate regression, public output drift, and late evidence. `evaluateScheduleWindow` enforces idempotency with duplicate detection and late delivery rejection. `buildHealthDecision` appends decisions without editing historical gate decisions. `buildHealthProjection` creates deterministic projections. `evaluateMonitorRecovery` resumes from requirements/health-decision/incident/projection/complete with `CERT-HEALTH-02` ambiguous state. `isHealthTransitionValid` validates state transitions. No silent overwrite of newer health decisions, no monitor failure masquerading as current health.

CERT-009 clean cutover at `packages/werkstatt/src/certification/cutover/` owns the single-site clean cutover marker and legacy state prohibition. `CleanCutoverMarkerV1` contains new candidate, all decision IDs (dev, alt, main verification, evaluator), dossier root, Main identity (candidate, artifact hash, deployment URL, timestamp), health state, rollback target identity, bootstrap exception closure, continuous health window completion, and deterministic marker hash. `verifyCutover` rejects legacy state reads for success (`CERT-CUTOVER-01`), missing dev/alt/main/evaluator decisions (`CERT-CUTOVER-02`..`05`), incomplete health window (`CERT-CUTOVER-06`), revoked health (`CERT-CUTOVER-07`), same rollback candidate (`CERT-CUTOVER-08`), and invalid component set hash (`CERT-CUTOVER-09`). `checkLegacyStateProhibition` enforces no runtime command reads legacy release certification, grace, or mission artifacts for success. `verifyMarkerIntegrity` detects tampering via hash recomputation. Bootstrap rollback target is protected until exception is closed; prior-certified targets are always protected.

agent-runtime-architecture.transition: Current `werkstatt/plugin@1` source remains until packet 230; no compatibility adapter is introduced.

layer.role: Layer 1: P2P replication of the platform monorepo across workshops. Standard git protocols (fetch/merge --ff-only) with commit signature verification (RFC-0560). Commands: gitmesh.sync, gitmesh.status, gitmesh.verify.

rules.rule: gitmesh.sync is pull-only — never pushes to remotes.
Convergence uses highest committer timestamp among remote-tracking branches.
gitmesh.status is a local-only query — no network I/O.
gitmesh.verify is incremental — only new commits since last verification are checked.
